name: Solve similar triangles
seoDesc: Solve similar triangles: work out α (First triangle dimensions) from the B and the A. A free math calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the B and the A and the Solve similar triangles calculator solves for α (First triangle dimensions). Think of it as a shortcut for a homework check, a spreadsheet build or a bit of mental arithmetic you want to confirm. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the Solve similar triangles calculator work?
sections.html:
The Solve similar triangles calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports α (First triangle dimensions) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the given and the angle you know); then you type in the b (First triangle dimensions), the b (First triangle dimensions), a (Second triangle dimensions) and a (Second triangle dimensions).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Solve similar triangles calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Α=(((1 ÷ 2) × (-(A ^ 2) + (B ^ 2) + (C ^ 2)) ÷ (B × C)))
Β=(((1 ÷ 2) × ((A ^ 2) − (B ^ 2) + (C ^ 2)) ÷ (A × C)))
Γ=(((1 ÷ 2) × ((A ^ 2) + (B ^ 2) − (C ^ 2)) ÷ (A × B)))
B=C × the cosine of (Α) + the square root of ((A ^ 2) − (C ^ 2) × (the sine of (Α), 2))
Β=((1 ÷ 2) × ((A ^ 2) − (B ^ 2) + (C ^ 2)) ÷ (A × C))
C=the square root of ((A ^ 2) − 2 × A × B × the cosine of (Γ) + (B ^ 2))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Read it as a template. Every number above can be replaced with one of yours; only the relationship between them is fixed.

  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: α = 60 deg, β = 60 deg and γ = 60 deg should be roughly the size you expected from Given set to angle and 2 sides and Angle you know set to α.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Solve similar triangles calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Settling an argument about a number with a quick, traceable result
  • Checking a homework answer before you hand it in
  • Splitting a bill, a measurement or a shape problem between several people
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the B and the A — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Solve similar triangles calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns α (First triangle dimensions), derived from the B and the A. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Solve similar triangles calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the B and the A, which is 16 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter a (First triangle dimensions) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. A (First triangle dimensions) opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports α = 60 deg. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Solve similar triangles calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
